title: Pump-pressure measurement filtering
equipment: Centrifugal pump, discharge-pressure transmitter, and recycle control valve
physicalPurpose: Hold discharge pressure while reducing vibration-noise-driven recycle-valve movement without hiding unacceptable response lag.
principalTechnique: Bypass, first-order, and cascaded second-order measurement-filter comparison
objective: Configure bypass, first-order, and cascaded second-order measurement paths for the same simulated centrifugal-pump pressure loop; predict their discrete first-sample response and frequency attenuation; use three equivalent retained runs to select the weakest filter that satisfies the declared pressure-noise and recycle-valve-activity requirements without exceeding the allowed measurement-path lag or final-window pressure bias; and explain why smoothing cannot reconstruct information lost before sampling.

simplifications: The hydraulic process is one local FOPDT pressure-deviation state.
Measurement noise is deterministic approximate normal broadband noise and does not move the simulated plant state.
A duplicate noiseless simulator plant exposes evidence-only true pressure; the controller never reads that channel and a physical installation normally cannot provide it.
The declared 0.001 bar resolution is metadata; no separate quantizer is added.
Pump curves, resonance, cavitation, valve stiction, sensor dynamics, aliasing before sampling and correlated noise are omitted.

baseline.limitation: Broadband transmitter noise reaches PI feedback and creates unnecessary recycle-valve movement.

change.decision: Run bypass, one pole, and two cascaded poles with the same deterministic noise and change no plant, controller, timing, event, axis, or limit; select the fewest poles satisfying attenuation, lag, and bias requirements. Filter selection is initialization-only and requires a restart.

disturbances: The same seeded 0.02 bar standard-deviation measurement-noise sequence is active in every run

abortPredicates: SP, raw PV, controller PV or MV is nonfinite
Seed, plant, PI, initial state, event, duration, scale or timing differs between runs
safety.restorationMode: Return pressure-deviation SP to zero and select Manual at 0 percent recycle-valve trim
simulationOnlyRestrictions: Physical filter changes require recorded spectra, stability review, topology approval, and immediate authorization.

video.viewerOutcome: Explain first- and second-order measurement filtering and select a filter from reproducible noise, valve-activity, and lag evidence.
requiredVisibleEvidence: continuous reference and executed discrete cutoff distinction
RMS, travel, lag and bias table

learning.context: Setpoint weighting changed reference response but cannot prevent a pressure controller from reacting to vibration and electrical noise in its measurement.
learning.reason: Measurement noise causes unnecessary recycle-valve movement; filtering may reduce it but adds lag and phase loss, so smooth appearance alone cannot justify a filter.
theory: A spectrum describes content by frequency; quantization rounds values to finite increments, while the seeded simulator noise is broadband measurement variation rather than plant motion.
A first-order low-pass satisfies tau times filtered derivative plus filtered value equals input, with cutoff 1 over 2 pi tau and approximately 20 dB per decade high-frequency roll-off.
Two cascaded identical stages approach 40 dB per decade roll-off and add more attenuation, phase loss and lag.
Filtering after sampling cannot undo aliasing; controller-PV increment RMS, MV increment RMS, tracking error and integrated raw-minus-controller lag measure different trade-offs.
learning.workedPrediction: With dt=tau=0.1 s, the shipped filter coefficient is 2/3: a 0.10 bar jump produces 0.0667 bar after one stage and 0.0444 bar after the second. The continuous reference cutoff is 1.5915 Hz, while the executed one-stage and cascaded discrete minus-three-decibel frequencies are about 1.9591 and 1.2118 Hz below the 5 Hz Nyquist frequency.
practicalPreparation: Inspect the pump, pressure transmitter, recycle valve, noise source, signals, units, operating point, limits and safe state.
Calculate coefficient, cutoff, Nyquist and first-sample responses; verify one seed and identical plant, PI, event, timing, axes and limits before three approved fresh runs.
learning.baseline: Bypass filtering, establish 0 bar for 5 s, step to 1 bar, and retain raw/controller PV, MV, pressure error, increment RMS and sampled-loop lag.
learning.change: Repeat with one pole and then two cascaded poles at tau 0.1 s, changing only filter selection.
learning.comparison: Compare controller-PV increment RMS 0.02549, 0.01463 and 0.00891 bar; applied-valve increment RMS 0.01787, 0.01028 and 0.00628 percentage points; total travel 2.88, 1.67 and 1.03 percentage points; and aligned lag area 0.0000, 0.0486 and 0.0983 bar-seconds.
learning.validation: Require candidate pressure and valve attenuation ratios no greater than 0.80, lag area no greater than 0.08 bar-seconds, final-window absolute mean controller error no greater than 0.05 bar, identical reproduced noise, finite signals and bounded applied MV; select the fewest passing poles.
learning.explanation: Explain why extra poles reduce noise-driven activity while increasing measurement-path lag, why the first-order candidate is the weakest qualifying filter, and why the smoother second-order trace is rejected by its lag requirement; derivative-specific noise amplification remains deferred.
learning.transfer: For another measurement, inspect spectrum and resolution, choose cutoff relative to process bandwidth and sample rate, calculate discrete coefficients, and compare equal recorded or seeded runs using both noise/activity and lag/robustness evidence.
